title: Microsoft Intune: Administrator protection settings in the settings catalog and account protection template
summary: The briefing's actionable claims are supported, including the settings catalog route, Intune licensing and the Windows security baseline default exception. The Graph call is correctly limited to creating a policy rather than enabling Administrator protection. Minor corrections remain to the wizard route and the checklist's coverage in the controls table.

claims.quote: Adminless settings able to be configured in settings catalog and account protection template.

claims.claim: The roadmap description is one sentence and does not define Adminless.
claims.quote: Adminless settings able to be configured in settings catalog and account protection template.

claims.claim: The cited Learn pages do not identify Adminless as the roadmap's name for Administrator protection.
claims.quote: Searched: "Adminless" "Administrator protection" Intune. Read Administrator protection, settings catalog, Account protection and Intune What's new; none explicitly equates the names.

claims.claim: Administrator protection is a Windows 11 platform feature keeping users deprivileged until just-in-time elevation is needed.
claims.quote: This feature operates on the principle of least privilege, keeping users in a deprivileged state and granting just-in-time elevation rights only when needed.

claims.claim: The isolated admin token is issued to the requesting process.
claims.quote: This token is issued to the requesting process and is destroyed once the process ends, ensuring that admin privileges don't persist.

claims.fix: Include the wizard progression documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-configuration/settings-catalog/: 'Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy > Windows 10 and later > Settings catalog > Create > Basics > Configuration settings > Add settings > Local Policies Security Options > User Account Control Type Of Admin Approval Mode'. The catalog page supports the initial route and is already cited; the linked Administrator protection page supports the final category and setting. The pre-check's missing words are therefore not a wrong-path finding.

claims.where: Governance guidance; Governance controls: checklist-to-table gap
claims.claim: The checklist tells readers to review LAPS targeting and security baselines, capture elevation events and review policy status, but the table has no rows for these controls.
claims.quote: Check whether your Windows security baselines already set ... Capture elevation events 15031 and 15032 ... The checklist's Intune LAPS targeting review, Windows security baseline check, elevation-event capture and Intune policy-status review have no corresponding row in the controls table.
claims.fix: The Before rollout LAPS-targeting and Windows-security-baseline checks and the After rollout elevation-event capture and Intune-policy-status review lack table rows. Acknowledging that gap does not meet the checklist rule. Remove those four checklist instructions; retain their already-supported factual explanations in the body. Do not add unverified control rows.
